To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine the nature of the stationary points, find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at the x-coordinates of the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, the stationary point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the stationary point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
